question.text: Sona Fund (Cat I, 5-yr): Committed Capital INR 80 crore (fully called), Hurdle 10% compounded, Management Fee 1.5% on GAV incl. GST 18%, Set-up cost INR 2 cr amortised over 5 yr, yearly expenses INR 48 lakh, Incentive Fee 15%. Year-1 GAV = INR 92.8 cr. What is the Year-1 Net Asset Value (pre-incentives) closest to?

explanation.text: The Logic: GAV INR 92.80 cr. Less: set-up amortised INR 0.40 cr (2/5). Less: yearly expenses INR 0.48 cr. Less: Mgmt fee = 1.5% x 92.80 x 1.18 = INR 1.6426 cr. NAV pre-incentive = 92.80 - 0.40 - 0.48 - 1.6426 = INR 90.2774 cr ≈ INR 90.27 crore. Mirrors chapter Example 6.3 and 6.4 (Best Case). The Trap: B and C strip too many costs; D is the pre-expense GAV. Cross-Exam Context: Chapter 6 Examples 6.3/6.4 worked exactly this way. XIX-C tests the same computation pattern. Manager's Pro-Tip: Always present LPs with a 'GAV to NAV bridge': each line (set-up amortisation, operating expense, management fee, GST) makes it transparent. Opaque 'net-of-expense' figures erode LP trust.
